BiblicalUsage: mashsheh is a debt, and it occurs once, in Deuteronomy 15:2. There the manner of the release is that every creditor who lends to his neighbour shall release it, because it is called the LORD's release. The word is the debt that must be let go.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mashsheh shows me that God sets a limit on debt, and that release is part of His law, not only His grace.
